title: Sample Test 1: Aptitude + Technical
description: A 4-question mixed practice test: 2 aptitude and 2 technical MCQs.

questions.question: A laptop is sold at a 20% discount on its list price and still earns a profit of 20% on cost. The list price is what percent above the cost price?
questions.explanation: Let cost = 100. Selling price = 120 (20% profit). SP is 80% of list price, so list = 120 / 0.8 = 150. Markup over cost = 150 - 100 = 50%.

questions.question: A can finish a job alone in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. In how many more days will B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 of the job per day. In 4 days they finish 20/36 = 5/9. Remaining 4/9 at B's rate 1/18 per day takes (4/9) x 18 = 8 days.

questions.question: In a relational database, adding an index on a frequently filtered column has which primary trade-off?
options: It slows down reads but speeds up writes and reduces total storage used.
It speeds up read queries on that column but increases storage use and slows down inserts, updates and deletes.
It guarantees ACID compliance for every transaction on the table.
It removes the need for a primary key on the table.
questions.correctAnswer: It speeds up read queries on that column but increases storage use and slows down inserts, updates and deletes.
questions.explanation: An index is an extra sorted structure (usually a B-tree) that lets the engine find rows without a full scan, so reads on that column get faster. Every write must also maintain that structure, which costs time and extra storage.

questions.question: You find the middle node of a singly linked list with the slow/fast two-pointer technique. What are the time and extra-space complexities?
options: O(n log n) time, O(1) extra space
questions.explanation: The fast pointer moves two nodes for every one node the slow pointer moves, so the slow pointer lands on the middle after about n/2 steps. Only two pointers are kept, so extra space is constant.
